acceptance_criteria.criterion: checkRevalidationGuard forwards activeStages (or DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES fallback) to getUpstreamTypes
New test validates the fix with a custom-stages WP where upstream rework occurs on a non-default stage
npm test passes — all existing + new tests green

summary: Fixed checkRevalidationGuard in workflow-helpers.ts to forward activeStages to getUpstreamTypes (line ~209). Added PipelineType import to workflow-helpers.test.ts and a new test 'fires when security-audit rework occurs after qa PASS (custom activeStages)' that validates the fix with 5-stage custom WP. npm run build passes, npm test passes (1273 tests, 0 failures).

comments.note: The fix required only one token change in workflow-helpers.ts (line ~209): getUpstreamTypes(pipelineType) → getUpstreamTypes(pipelineType, activeStages ?? DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES). The activeStages parameter was already threaded through to hasDownstreamFail but was silently ignored for the upstream type lookup — a subtle omission that could cause false negatives for custom-stage WPs.

summary: All 4 acceptance criteria verified. (1) workflow-helpers.ts line 209 confirmed: getUpstreamTypes(pipelineType, activeStages ?? DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES) — activeStages forwarded with DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES fallback. (2) New test at workflow-helpers.test.ts line 495 exercises a 5-stage custom WP with security-audit rework invalidating code-review — correctly fires the guard. (3) npm run build: 0 errors. (4) npm test: 1273 tests, 0 failures across 41 test files (includes the new test).

comments.note: The one-line fix at workflow-helpers.ts line 209 is minimal and correct: getUpstreamTypes(pipelineType, activeStages ?? DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES). The null-coalescing fallback preserves backward compatibility for default-stage WPs. No behavioral change for the common 4-stage path.

New test (workflow-helpers.test.ts line 495) accurately targets the regression: a 5-stage custom WP where security-audit re-runs after code-review FAIL. The test comment block explains exactly why the guard would silently skip before the fix vs correctly fire after. High-quality test.

summary: Phase 1 Step 2 — checkRevalidationGuard activeStages forwarding fix reviewed and approved. The one-line change (getUpstreamTypes now receives activeStages ?? DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES instead of no argument) closes a silent false-negative gap for custom-stage WPs. The ?? fallback is correct given the optional parameter signature. Companion regression test at workflow-helpers.test.ts line ~495 documents the before/after behavior clearly. No blocking issues.

comments.note: Minor style asymmetry: hasDownstreamFail (line 206) passes activeStages directly (undefined propagates to the callee's default), while getUpstreamTypes (line 209) uses activeStages ?? DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES (explicit fallback). Both are functionally correct — both callees handle undefined safely. For consistency, consider applying the same ?? pattern to hasDownstreamFail, but this is a non-blocking style observation.

New test at workflow-helpers.test.ts line ~495 is high quality: the comment block explicitly contrasts the old broken behavior (DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES misses security-audit) vs. the fixed behavior (customStages correctly includes it), making the regression scenario self-documenting.
